topic: Professor L.S. Fan’s Legacy at Ohio State
title: Professor L.S. Fan’s Legacy at Ohio State
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: During his 45-year tenure at Ohio State Chemical Engineering, Professor Fan left his mark at every aspect of the department. As an educator, as a researcher, as a leader and as a mentor, he led the department to new heights and set very high standards for his colleagues and his students to aspire to. After 45 years, he continues to shine as a bright guiding light for all of us. Reflections on his impact on our profession and on the Ohio State Chemical Engineering will be shared.

topic: Prof. L.-S. Fan’s Impacts on Industries - in Honor of the 2022 Receipt of the Warren K. Lewis Award
title: Prof. L.-S. Fan’s Impacts on Industries - in Honor of the 2022 Receipt of the Warren K. Lewis Award
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: Prof. L.-S. Fan received the 2022 AIChE Warren K. Lewis Award to recognize his distinguished and continuing contributions to chemical engineering education, which is one of the most prestigious awards for education in chemical engineering. Prof. Fan has published many high-quality journal papers, patents and books including the widely adapted textbooks. He also spends extensive efforts for educational outreach activities, i.e., in various academic societies, science and engineering fairs, advisory board/editor of multiple scientific journals, mentoring young engineering faculty, advising over 200 graduate students and post-doctoral associates. Besides all these educational efforts in academic, Prof. Fan has also had a remarkable impact on industry. As either previous students or scholars from Prof. Fan’s group, we will talk about Prof. Fan’s impacts on different areas in industry including chemicals, oil/gas, clean energy, etc. The presenters are but not limit to the following: Ye-Mon Chen, Shell and Quad County Corn Processors Ping Cai, W.R. Grace Bing Du, ExxonMobil Technology & Engineering Company Zhe Cui, Shell Global Solutions Luis G. Velazquez Vargas, The Babcock and Wilcox Company

topic: Impact of Professor. L.-S. Fan’s Scholarship Endeavors Research on Indian Chemical Society
title: Impact of Professor. L.-S. Fan’s Scholarship Endeavors Research on Indian Chemical Society
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: Prof. L.-S. Fan is a renowned researcher in particle science and technology, and multiphase reaction engineering with impact on many aspects of chemical engineering including energy and environmental systems as applied to such operations as resid hydrotreating and flue gas cleaning using gas-liquid-solid fluidized bed reactors, and hydrogen production from acid gas in natural gas using fixed bed reactors. He is also a highly respected scholar and educator who, besides being an excellent classroom teacher, has devoted much of his energy to mentoring undergraduate and graduate students and postdoctoral researchers and younger colleagues. The impact of his scholarship has been global and has been significant and included Indian chemical engineering community. His receipt of the prestigious AIChE Warren K Lewis Award for Chemical Engineering Education is a befitting recognition of his many outstanding contributions to education and rightfully cements his position as a top chemical engineering educator in the US. Professor Fan's exceptional mentorship for Indian students at the PhD level has been just as remarkable as his contributions to the research field in chemical engineering. He has actively engaged with Indian students, welcoming them into his research group and advising over 40 Indian students for their PhD dissertation research. This has positively impacted the Indian community by fostering the development of future researchers in the field. This presentation will encompass the remarks garnered from both current and previous Indian students who have grown under Prof. Fan's guidance, highlighting his influence on shaping the next generation of researchers. The insights of several most influential stalwarts in Indian academia who have worked with Prof. Fan over the years for the development of a better worldwide community through education will also be included. Professor Fan's groundbreaking innovations in clean fossil energy conversion processes have significantly reduced harmful emissions of CO2, SO2, and NOx while enabling the production of electricity, syngas, hydrogen, chemicals, and liquid fuels. His redox chemical looping technology research has been particularly impactful in India's steel industry, contributing significantly to the decarbonization of steel production through the development of efficient and sustainable processes. With his commitment to achieving a net-zero carbon future, Prof. Fan has expanded his scope globally, developing clean energy conversion technologies that have the potential to benefit the global steel industry in the fight against climate change. The impact of his work as evidenced through testimonials from experts who have witnessed the mitigation of emissions and increased process efficiency as a result of his research, will also be given in this presentation. In recognition of his exceptional contributions to the field of chemical engineering, Prof. Fan was elected as a member of the prestigious Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE) in 2019, in addition to holding memberships of other national academies. Overall, this presentation highlights the significant impact of Prof. Fan's scholarships through his career long education and research endeavors on the academic and industrial development of India, particularly in the areas of environmental engineering and clean energy conversion technologies.

topic: Liquid-Solid and Gas-Liquid-Solid Circulating Fluidized Beds (G-LSCFB) and Their Applications
title: Liquid-Solid and Gas-Liquid-Solid Circulating Fluidized Beds (G-LSCFB) and Their Applications
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: Although gas-solid circulating fluidized beds (GSCFB) have been around for over 70 years, liquid-solid circulating fluidized beds (LSCFB) and gas-liquid-solid circulating fluidized beds (GLSCFB) have only got the attention of researchers since the mid-1990s. Compared to the well-studied GSCFB riser, (G)LSCFB has some distinctively different characteristics, such as more uniform axial and radial flow structure, non-obvious cluster structure, a wide range of operable solids holdups, low fluid (liquid and gas) velocity and excellent mass and heat transfer. Through a series of studies in this group since 1996, as well as efforts from several other groups worldwide, fundamental understandings on LSCFB and GLSCFB have been achieved. This talk will provide a general overview on the industrial applications and potential applications of LSCFB and GLSCFB.

topic: Looping and Succession for Energy Environmental Education
title: Looping and Succession for Energy Environmental Education
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: Professor L-S Fan is a renowned scholar and educator in the field of chemical engineering and has made significant contributions to the advancement of the discipline. He is a foreign member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, and has significantly promote the scholarly exchanges between the United States and China. Additionally, Professor Fan has mentored a number of Chinese students and postdoctoral researchers who have gone on to pursue successful careers in academia and industry. Under his guidance, I have learned the key concepts and skills required of an independent researcher, including critical thinking, careful methodology, and technology innovation. This talk will highlight the ways in which Professor Fan's mentorship, support, and collaboration have impacted the development of Chinese students and scholars.

topic: A Career in Education: A Personal Reflection
title: A Career in Education: A Personal Reflection
session_title: In Honor of Prof. Liang-Shih Fan, the 2022 Recipient of the Warren K. Lewis Award II (Invited Talks)
abstract: I am grateful to the AIChE in bestowing upon me the Warren K Lewis Award for Chemical Engineering Education. I consider this award as the most significant professional honor that I have received. This is especially the case because, many years ago, when I embarked on a career in higher education, I set the goal of achieving excellence as an educator as my foremost aim. In receiving this recognition, I take immense satisfaction in feeling that I have achieved that aim. In pursuing this goal over all these years, I have been very fortunate to have met numerous highly distinguished scholars who mentored and supported me, guiding, influencing, and shaping me into the educator that I eventually became. They have served as exceptional role models and inspired me to assume the same role for my younger colleagues and my students. In fact, their specific impact on me has extended well beyond my pedagogical goals to influence my endeavors in research, professional service, and entrepreneurship. I am privileged to name some of them here: C. C. Chen (my BS advisor), C. Y. Wen (my PhD advisor), L.T. Fan (my post-doc advisor and my cousin), Maurice Bergougnou, Bob Brodkey, John Davidson, Norman Epstein, Daizo Kunii, Norman Li, Charlie Shao-Lee Soo, Barry Tarmy, Chi Tien, Danny I.C. Wang, Jimmy Wei, Mooson Kwauk, and Jack Zakin. During my career at Ohio State, I have been most fortunate to have worked with a large number of undergraduate students, graduate students and post-doctoral research associates. I have found it gratifying to observe the development of their own individual careers in the years that followed their departure from my lab, whether in industry or academia. I have been privileged to mentor students at other universities where I serve as honorary professor, namely Tsinghua University in China and National Taiwan University in Taiwan. This enrichment that comes with student interaction has also excitingly extended to universities where I spent sabbatical leave including, Cambridge University in UK, Hannover University in Germany, and ETH in Switzerland. One of my goals, in addition to fostering and supporting the learning of the students in my classes, has been to combine the cultivation of the intellects and technical skills of each of my students with the assuredness of a deep commitment to an ethic of professionalism, so that each one of them will be a powerful force to the profession they serve and the society they live in. I am proud to note that many of my advisees have been very successful in academia and industry and their continued success and achievement fills me with gratitude. I can devote much of the energy needed to pursue my career because of the full support of my wife. Our collective endeavors in exercising our shared passion for education have also affected our children in their choice of professional careers. Both my son and my daughter have established themselves in academia as professors in their respective fields. A successful educator complements and combines inspiring teaching that effectively delivers classroom material with innovative research, scholarship and leadership, creating knowledge with insights, breakthroughs, and inventions that are ultimately embedded as new learning materials for generations to come and which benefit society at large. In receiving this honor, I am reminded once again of how deeply indebted I am to those who helped to illuminate my path as an educator desirous of impacting the discipline and the profession in a meaningful way, and to my students and younger colleagues who continually make me a better educator. I recognize all of them here with deep and abiding gratitude.
